secondary_sources: ASMI — Southeast Alaska Seafood Export Value Reports
_provenance.notes: Southeast Alaska (SEAK) comprises the Alaska Panhandle — a 500-mile arc of islands, fjords, and rainforest from Yakutat south to Ketchikan. The region produces the highest-value commercial salmon per fish in Alaska via the troll fleet (Chinook/Coho hook-and-line). Primary commercial salmon fisheries: seine (pink/chum), troll (Chinook/Coho), and gillnet. The region's seafood industry generates approximately $880M in annual ex-vessel value across salmon, crab, halibut, herring, and dive species. Major ports: Sitka, Ketchikan, Petersburg, Juneau, Wrangell, Craig.

primary_ports.primary_species: Salmon troll, Dungeness crab, Sea cucumber
